# dsh-emacs-bridge

This is a two-way bridge between
GNU Emacs and the
DeepSeek Harness
(DSH).  It lets you control DSH

from Emacs, including submitting
prompts, reading replies, and controlling sessions.  The Emacs-side
user interface is designed to closely follow Emacs conventions.
## Installation

The bridge consists of two components: a DeepSeek Harness plugin
(`dsh-emacs-bridge`), and an Emacs

package to interact with the
harness.  The package ships the baseline library `dsh-bridge.el` plus
a

n optional companion, `dsh-bridge-extras.el`; the baseline never
loads the companion on its own.
### Requirements

- `dsh`, the DeepSeek Harness.
- `pnpm` installed on the executable path (DSH uses it to install plu

gins).
- GNU Emacs, version 29 or later, installed on the executable path.
- (Recommended) The Markd
own mode Emacs package.  From Emacs, install it via `M-x package-install RET markdown-mode RET`.
### Installing via the DSH Plugin Manager

1. From the DSH web interface, click **Plugins** in the left panel,
then **Add Plugin** at the upper

right.  Enter `dsh-emacs-bridge`
into the box, and click **Install**.  When it finishes, click

## Usage
From Emacs, the main entry-points are these two commands:

* `M-x dsh-bridge` — open a transient menu for DSH commands.
* `M-x dsh-bridge-list-sessions` — show
a list of DSH sessions.

### Transient menu

The `M-x dsh-bridge` command opens a transient menu that prompts for
the next command.  The menu's t

op line shows the session to be acted
on (chosen based on your recent activity); you can cycle throu

gh
available sessions with `M-p`/`M-n`.

Type `RET` to perform the default interaction on the session.  For
example, if the session is runnin

g, this command opens a view buffer
to show the replies; if the session is idle, it opens a prompt b

uffer
as well as a view buffer (if there are replies).

## Security Matters

The DSH-Emacs bridge listens on the DSH web server's loopback
interface.  It never contacts a third-

party service.  Every route is
gated by a shared bearer token, generated on first use and stored wit

h
owner-only permissions at `~/.dsh/dsh-bridge-token`.  Emacs reads that
file directly, and the plug

in fetches it from a route fenced to
loopback peers and same-origin pages.  Any third party with acc

ess to
the token can do everything this Emacs package can (send prompts, read
session logs, answer q
ueries and approval requests, etc.).

Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB, and messages waiting for Emacs sit
in a bounded outbox.  The tur

n activity reporter, `/turns`, carries at
most 500 of the latest activity entries per turn, and acti

vity for at
most the newest 40 turns; it remains summary-only.  The optional detail
inspector's read

-only `/details/item` route is the one place that serves
complete committed reasoning, raw tool argu

ments, result content, and
durable per-call diff fragments.  It is bearer-authenticated and
loopback

-only like every other route, is fetched only for an activity
item at point or an explicit inspector

refresh/page, and never travels
over SSE.  Its bounds are user-visible in the inspector section abo

ve:
64 KiB text pages, 256 KiB diff input per side, and 128 KiB of rendered
diff text.  Provider `AU

TH` failure diagnostics
remain suppressed exactly as they are in `/turns`; malformed or
unreadable d

iff metadata is labeled `unavailable` rather than decoded
loosely.

The *Install Emacs package* button in the plugin configuration card is
the one place that spawns a p

rocess.  Clicking it runs `emacs` in
batch mode, with fixed arguments, to install the bundled versio

ned
package directory (the baseline library, the optional companion, and
the generated package descr

iptor) into the [Emacs packaging
system](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/P

e [Emacs packaging
system](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/emacs/Packages.html).
